The project configuration files `prj.conf` and `boards/pocketbeagle_2_am6254_a53.conf` unconditionally set `CONFIG_MAX_THREAD_BYTES`. When the test is built for a non-userspace configuration, this results in a Kconfig warning because the dependency on `CONFIG_USERSPACE` is not met.

The fix is to remove the `CONFIG_MAX_THREAD_BYTES` setting from these configuration files. This will resolve the warning. For userspace builds, the system will use the default value for `CONFIG_MAX_THREAD_BYTES`, which may result in slightly higher memory usage but ensures the test remains functional and the build is warning-free.

The root cause of the Kconfig warning is that `CONFIG_MAX_THREAD_BYTES` is being set in configuration files, but this option is only available when `CONFIG_USERSPACE` is enabled. The test is designed to run in both userspace and non-userspace (supervisor) modes. A review of the source code shows that this test does not use thread-local storage (TLS), which is what `CONFIG_MAX_THREAD_BYTES` controls. Therefore, this configuration is not necessary for the test to function correctly.

The fix is to remove the `CONFIG_MAX_THREAD_BYTES` setting from both the project's main configuration file (`prj.conf`) and the board-specific overlay (`pocketbeagle_2_am6254_a53.conf`). This resolves the warning for non-userspace builds and has no negative impact on userspace builds since the feature is unused.
